world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Fluckiger, Cheryl A. 1987. Phonological sketch: Kuo. Yaoundé: SIL Cameroon. 9 pp. (typescript, scanned, no text layer; scanned at 200 dpi one page at a time)
sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: open copy online
sources.note: Nothing on stress or accent. Sect. 5 'Tone patterns' (p. 8): three level tones (high, mid unmarked, low) plus one rising tone; one tone marked per morpheme; the rising tone is contrastive only on a limited number of CVV/CVC morphemes; tone patterns 'group into certain fairly predictable classes (see Camburn, n.d.)'. Sects. 2-4 give morpheme shapes (CV, CVV, CVC, CVCV...), consonants and vowels. No word 'stress', 'accent' or 'prominence' anywhere in the 9 pages.

sources.citation: Glidden, Suellyn H. 1985. The Koh verbal system. Work Papers of the Summer Institute of Linguistics, University of North Dakota Session 29: 223-282. doi:10.31356/silwp.vol29.04
sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: open copy online (also: harvard online access (harvardkey))
sources.note: Sect. 1.4 'Basic phonology' (p. 227) lists 35 phonemes and states: 'Koh has three level tones: high, mid, and low... There is also a rising contour tone... There is one phonemic tone per morpheme. Tone is marked on the first vowel of each morpheme.' Also a word-level nasalization prosody. No mention of stress or accent anywhere in the 62-page paper (grep for stress/accent/prominence: none). Fn. 1 (p. 279): 'The phonological analysis of Koh is being done by my colleague, Ms. J. Camburn.'

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid page kuoo1238 and reference records (accessed 2026-09-17)
sources.note: Bibliography only: Fluckiger 1987 (phonological sketch), Glidden 1984/1985, Elders 2006, Ubels & Ubels 1980 (Karang), Bennett 1983, Boyd & Pasch 1988 (classification). No stress statement.

sources.citation: Wikipedia, 'Kuo language' (accessed 2026-09-17), citing Fluckiger 1987, ALCAM 2012 and a 2017 Kuo literature-committee primer
sources.note: Gives consonant/vowel inventory and 'Kuo has 4 tones, written using tone accent (except for mid tone is unwritten)'. Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Ubels, Edward H. & Virginia Ubels. 1980. Phonology of Karang. Yaoundé: SIL mimeo.
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.access_detail: not located online or at Harvard
sources.note: Karang is the closest well-described relative (Central Mbum); Fluckiger 1987 models the Kuo analysis on Karang (vowel length vs. sequences, orthography). A prosody/stress statement for Karang would be the nearest proxy for the subgroup, though not a Kuo statement.

sources.citation: Camburn, Jan. n.d. [c. 1985-1987]. Preliminary notes on Kuo phonology / phonological analysis of Koh. Yaoundé or N'Djaména: SIL manuscript.
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.note: The only fuller phonological analysis of Kuo that exists: Fluckiger 1987 credits Camburn for the preliminary phonology and the tone-class analysis, and Glidden 1985 (fn. 1) says the phonological analysis of Koh 'is being done by my colleague, Ms. J. Camburn'. If any Kuo source discusses stress/prominence, it is this one. Not listed by Glottolog; may exist only in the SIL Cameroon/Chad archives.
